_comment: Test fixture loaded by tests/run-tests.sh via --settings. --settings MERGES on top of the developer's live ~/.claude/settings.json — it does not replace it. We rely on the merge to override only the fields listed under _intentional_diffs_from_live (primarily disabling the Telegram hook). Drift detection in tests/check-structure.sh (Phase 7) enforces that NO OTHER fields differ, so the merge produces predictable behaviour. To change live settings, edit ~/.claude/settings.json and re-run check-structure.sh; it will tell you if the fixture needs updating.
_intentional_diffs_from_live: hooks.Notification: emptied (live: notify-telegram.sh) — primary mechanism: tests should not ping Telegram. Fixture's empty array overrides live's populated array via the merge.
hooks.Stop: empty list (matches current live state; kept explicit as a contract — if Stop hook returns to live, this still suppresses it during tests)

env.CLAUDE_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: omitted from fixture (live has it). Note: --settings is additive, so the live value still leaks through at test time. This is harmless because no hook script is left to consume it; documented here so drift detection's expected diff set stays accurate.
env.CLAUDE_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID: same as CLAUDE_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN — leaks through merge, harmless without a hook to consume it.
